fix_round_preregistration.expectation: The original fixture only showed 'prune found nothing to act on', which cannot distinguish selective preservation from doing nothing at all. Adding a worktree whose branch IS merged into the default branch (so it is a real prune candidate) alongside the crash/dirty/unrelated worktree will let prune actually remove one and leave the other, producing a genuine contrast.
fix_round_preregistration.criteria: In one repo: a worktree merged into the default branch (a real prune candidate), plus a separate dirty/unmerged worktree (must be preserved). Run wt step prune --min-age=0s (to bypass the default 1-day age guard, since a just-created worktree looks 'merged' but is too young by default) and confirm the merged worktree's directory and branch are removed while the dirty/unmerged worktree's files and branch are untouched.
